title: Proofs under the dossier
question: Keep the three Design / Supervision / FF&E cards as they are. How should the six commitments (Schedule → Implementation) sit underneath?

options.label: Single-stack atelier list
options.thesis: One quiet vertical stack — each proof is a full-measure row, not a 3-column grid. Reading rhythm, not a feature matrix.
options.viewport: Cards unchanged above; below, six ruled rows stacked in the shell with title left and body flowing beside or under.
options.risk: Longer scroll; needs tight vertical rhythm so it does not feel like another text wall.
options.case: Kills the 2×3 column look you dislike while keeping every factual commitment.

options.label: Horizontal proof strip
options.thesis: Six compact proof plates scroll sideways under the cards — same shell-align grammar as the dossier and team row.
options.viewport: Cards stay; a second horizontal track of shorter commitment tiles with title + short body.
options.risk: Two horizontal tracks can feel repetitive if the second is not clearly smaller.
options.case: Most continuous with the cards you like; commitments become browseable, not a grid.

options.label: Split dialogue
options.thesis: Left: one short hold line. Right: the six proofs as a single flowing column — Studio dialogue grammar, not a card grid.
options.viewport: Cards above; below a 2-column split with intro on the left and stacked proofs on the right.
options.risk: Needs a truthful intro line — no invented claims; can feel text-heavy on mobile when stacked.
